request.spec: Change the customerCode format to '<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>' where CITY3 is the upper-cased first three letters of the city, LAST3 the first three of the lastName, and NNNN a per-city 4-digit sequence (one more than the owners already in that city). Every value derived from the customerCode, such as the membership number, must be rebuilt on the new format. This changes the current customerCode and everything built from it.

agent.result_text:
All tests pass (BUILD SUCCESS). `AcceptanceTest` is the only runnable test class in this repo (the other files in the acceptance package are the abstract base and a helper).

## Summary

Changed the `customerCode` format from `<LAST3>-<NNNN>` to `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>`.

**`service/ClinicServiceImpl.java`** — reworked `nextCustomerCode`:
- Now takes the whole `Owner` (needs both city and lastName).
- Builds `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>`: upper-cased first 3 letters of `city`, first 3 of `lastName`, then a **per-city** 4-digit sequence = one more than the owners already in that city (city compared case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace via the existing `IdentityNormalizer`, matching the `countNamesakes`/`assignHousehold` pattern).
- Extracted a small `prefix3` helper for the shared "upper-cased first three letters" logic.
- Updated the call site to `nextCustomerCode(owner)`.

**Derived values:** `membershipNumber` in `mapper/OwnerMapper.java` is built by appending `-M<YY>` to `getCustomerCode()`, so it automatically rebuilds on the new format (e.g. `SYD-SMI-0007-M26`) — no code change needed there.

**`resources/openapi.yml`** — updated the `customerCode` and `membershipNumber` schema descriptions/examples to the new format.

The acceptance test `coreCustomerCodeHasCityPrefix` (asserting `[A-Z]{3}-[A-Z]{3}-\d{4}`) passes, along with the full suite.

code_review.final_verdict:
VERDICT: LGTM

The change slots cleanly into the existing structure:

- **Signature change matches the local idiom.** `nextCustomerCode(Owner)` now mirrors `countNamesakes(Owner)` — both take the whole `Owner` and read the fields they need. Passing the owner rather than plucking `lastName` out at the call site is the natural shape here, especially now that two fields (city and lastName) are needed.
- **Reuses the right existing utility.** City comparison goes through `IdentityNormalizer.normalize(...)`, exactly as `countNamesakes` and `assignHousehold` already do for names/addresses. The `findAll().stream().filter(...).count()` per-city counting pattern is the same shape as `countNamesakes`, so a maintainer reads it fluently. The differing filter fields make a shared abstraction unwarranted — extracting one would be over-abstraction.
- **`prefix3` extraction is well-judged.** The upper-cased-first-three-letters logic is now needed twice (city and lastName), so factoring it into a static private helper removes real duplication; making it `static` matches `deriveHouseholdId`. The Javadoc documents the null/short-value behavior.
- **Derived values rebuild for free, correctly left untouched.** `membershipNumber` in `OwnerMapper` is `customerCode + "-M" + yy`, so it picks up the new format with no code change — the spec's "everything built from it" is satisfied structurally without duplicating format knowledge. Not touching the mapper is the right call.
- **Docs kept in sync.** The method Javadoc and the OpenAPI description/examples (including the `membershipNumber` example) are updated to the new format, so no stale contract is left behind.

Logic sits in the right unit (code generation in the service, formatting in the mapper), nothing is duplicated, and no class is turning into a catch-all.
